chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Rifāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a person dyed with henna: if he is able to perform sajdah and recitation, may he perform salat in his henna? He said: Yes, if his cloth is tahir and he is in a state of wudu (ablution).

key_terms.الْمُخْتَضِبِ: a person using dye, especially henna
key_terms.خِرْقَتُهُ: his cloth or rag used in the dyeing context
key_terms.مُتَوَضِّئًا: being in a state of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can a person perform salat while wearing henna dye?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat while one is in a state of henna dyeing. It indicates permissibility so long as the person can perform the required acts of salat, his cloth is tahir, and he has wudu (ablution).
